articles.title: Paul Finebaum Calls for Firing of $72 Million 'Fraud' Head Coach After Week 4 Loss
articles.summary: Paul Finebaum called USC's Lincoln Riley a fraud on First Take and said the Trojans should pay his $72 million buyout after a 41-27 loss to Oregon in Week 4.
articles.body:
ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum said Monday that USC should fire head coach Lincoln Riley and eat a buyout worth about $72 million, two days after Oregon beat the Trojans 41-27 at the Coliseum in Week 4.

Finebaum spoke on ESPN's First Take while answering a question about the one-game suspension of USC linebacker Desman Stephens II. "I think everybody knows who the fraud is," Finebaum said. "It is Lincoln Riley."

Finebaum pointed to Clay Helton, the USC head coach the school fired in 2021.

"He has the same record at this point in his tenure as Clay Helton, who got fired and run off," Finebaum said. "It cost about $10 million to get rid of him. It will cost about $70 million to get rid of Lincoln Riley. But I promise you, USC people, it would be worth it because this guy is bringing your program down to the gutter."

Riley went 35-18 in his first four seasons at USC, which matched Helton's record through his first 53 games. He's now 39-19 with the Trojans.

The comments were a shift from Sunday. On The Matt Barrie Show, Finebaum said his take on Riley was "not going to be one of these, 'Lincoln Riley is a fraud. He should be fired.'"

"But I will tell you right now, Lincoln Riley is not an elite coach . He is not a coach capable of turning a program like Southern Cal around," Finebaum said. "I think he's a good coach. He was a better coach at Oklahoma than the Oklahoma fans now believe."

Finebaum is far from alone in the many calls questioning how much longer Riley's USC tenure will last.

Stephens hit Oregon quarterback Dante Moore in the head and chest with his shoulder as Moore slid at the end of an 11-yard run in the second quarter. Officials ejected the USC linebacker for targeting. Moore left on a backboard and was later diagnosed with a concussion.

Stephens was seen laughing and celebrating on the sideline after the hit. After the game, Riley was asked why Stephens was allowed to stay on the sideline. "Because he's on our football team," Riley said .

USC announced the suspension Sunday, so Stephens will miss Saturday's game against Washington. In a statement, Riley called his linebacker's actions " unacceptable ."

Finebaum ripped the timing of the punishment. "The fact that Lincoln Riley took until Sunday to decide to suspend Stephens, it's ridiculous," Finebaum said.

USC dropped six spots to No. 18 in the AP Top 25 after falling to 4-1 and 1-1 in the Big Ten. The Trojans are 5-15 against top-25 teams under Riley, and the fifth-year coach hasn't reached the College Football Playoff at USC.

Finebaum also took a shot at USC's place in its own city. "They don't even have the best team in Los Angeles right now," Finebaum said. "That belongs to UCLA."

UCLA is 4-0 and ranked No. 23 under first-year head coach Bob Chesney after a 54-3 win at Maryland in Week 4.

Washington visits USC on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 7:30 p.m. ET. The Trojans still face Penn State, Ohio State and Indiana later this season.

articles.title: Hart trusts Man City chair Al Mubarak over ruling
articles.summary: Former Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart believes club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak's claims they are innocent of breaking the Premier League's financial r...
articles.body:
Former Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart believes club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak's claims they are innocent of breaking financial rules.

City have been found guilty of the majority of 115 breaches of financial rules they had been accused of by the Premier League, although they are set to appeal against the ruling.

Al Mubarak said he is still committed to "proving the club's innocence" and the "process still has a long way to run".

Hart, who made 348 appearances for City in all competitions between 2006 and 2016, told BBC Radio 5 Live's Monday Night Club Al Mubarak was someone who has "led the club brilliantly" and is a person to "trust".

"I've heard everyone else go down every single rabbit hole, every single wormhole, every single discussion," Hart said.

"My honest opinion is I've got no reason not to trust Khaldoon. What he said is enough for me.

"I loved how he spoke. I loved the letter because that was from someone who cared about the club."

Hart twice won the Premier League (2011-12 and 2013-14) and League Cup (2013-14 and 2015-16) as well as the FA Cup (2010-11) during his time at City.

The 39-year-old said because there was "nothing concrete", it was matter of allowing things to "play out" and none of his achievements are in any way tarnished.

Hart added: "If Man City are found guilty, which I don't think they are because of what Khaldoon said, then there's conversations to be had.

"But right now I'm very confident and very, very calm. I'm very proud of what I've achieved and what I did with Manchester City and what we achieved as a team. And that doesn't change. That doesn't change until you tell me."

City were accused of a wide range of rule breaches, centering around claims they inflated sponsorship revenue from connected companies and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent financial regulations.

Hart said it hadn't "crossed my mind" to talk about the news with his former City team-mates because he "can't get involved in the ifs, buts and maybes".

"I did what I did. I lined up 11 v 11 and had it out on the pitch. I won some games, lost some games, drew some games, and I shook hands and I walked off," he said.

"I know what I did, I know what we did, and I know how it happened. It didn't feel like we were scheming or plotting."

articles.title: Can Wisconsin handle success? Fickell pushes team to continue grind after upset win
articles.summary: The Badgers beat a ranked team on the road last week. Now they have to reset and prepare for a Homecoming matchup with Michigan State.
articles.body:
MADISON – In the span of one week, Wisconsin 's situation has flipped.

The Badgers football team, fresh off a comeback win at Penn State , is a 10½-point favorite to beat Michigan State when they play Oct. 3 at Camp Randall Stadium (11:30 a.m. kickoff; Big Ten Network). Last week UW was a 10-point underdog against the Nittany Lions .

While point spreads aren't a true gauge of a team's talent, they are a sign of public sentiment, and the Badgers ' stock is on the rise after a big victory.

The key for the team will be to go about its business as if its a bear market.

"We're a team that has still continued to climb," Badgers coach Luke Fickell said Sept. 28 during his weekly press conference at Camp Randall Stadium. "Nothing has changed in the way we go about our business and so that's where for the first time, we've got to be able to handle some success and some positives and keep us going in the right direction."

The 24-20 win over Penn State gave the Badgers their first victory in Happy Valley since 2003 and snapped a six-game losing streak dating back to 2012 against the Nittany Lions overall.

The victory was also UW's highest-ranked win on the road since a 38-17 triumph at No. 9 Minnesota on Nov. 30, 2019.

That said, the film review probably brought the Badgers down to Earth, particularly the offense. In addition to Colton Joseph 's three interceptions, the Badgers committed five false-start penalties and were flagged a season-high nine times overall. Their third-down conversion rate of 26.7% (4 for 15) was also a season low.

"We know we've got to be able to play better," Fickell said. "And a lot of people will ask questions and point at the quarterback play. We know we have to play better, got to make better decisions at the quarterback position.

"But I think that there's a lot of other things that go into that. We've got to do a better job as a whole on helping our quarterback out. And so it's not just falling on the shoulders of the quarterback."

Wisconsin football schedule 2026, see Badgers' opponents, game dates

Fickell's respect for Michigan State Pat Fitzgerald runs deep

The Spartans come to town after suffering a 31-13 loss to Nebraska on Sept. 26 that also cost the team its top running back. First-year coach Pat Fitzgerald announced Sept. 28 that running back Cam Edwards will miss the remainder of the season due to what appeared to be a knee injury.

Edwards was one of the 62 newcomers Fitzgerald added to the program after he was hired in December.

Fitzgerald and Fickell played college ball at essentially the same time and have coached in the Big Ten for years as either a head coach or assistant.

That said, Fickell has respected Fitzgerald from afar due to his work at Northwestern and as president of the American Football Coaches Association.

"It's unique to see him not in the colors that he had worn for so many years," Fickell said. "But I know that he's building something, and I have the utmost respect for him."

Fickell praises impact of fans at Camp Randall Stadium

The matchup will be Wisconsin 's conference home opener and a chance to see what impact the Penn State victory has on fan attendance.

The announced attendance of 65,274 for the season opener was the lowest for the program since 1992. The attendance for Game 2 against Eastern Illinois was only slightly better (66,545).

This week UW will have a chance to ride the wave of that victory plus Homecoming weekend and what is expected to be good weather.

Fickell cited the environment of UW's last two home games – wins over Washington and Illinois last season – as examples of the positive impact the fans at Camp Randall can have on his team.

"Sometimes you think it's just if you can create a raucous environment like we were in last week, it makes it really difficult on the opposing team," Fickell said. "Well, you don't understand how much energy it gives to your team as well and so I think there's a balance there that we want to continue to create.

"We know we have a part in having success and playing better and putting the product out there that makes everybody excited to create those environments … Hopefully we can build upon the things that we've done and we'll have one of those this weekend."

articles.title: WVU vs Oklahoma St. Position Grades
articles.summary: Mountaineer fans, it’s time for the report card. We opened Big 12 play Saturday night against Oklahoma State with a lot of momentum. The Mountaineers entered...
articles.body:
Mountaineer fans, it's time for the report card.

We opened Big 12 play Saturday night against Oklahoma State with a lot of momentum. The Mountaineers entered the game 3-0, playing at home, with an offense that had been one of the most productive rushing attacks in the conference. For a while, it looked like we were going to make it four straight.

Then the tipped pass turned interception happened. I think everybody feels the same way I do, when I say that changed the momentum. We were about to go up 21 to 6, instead they went down and scored and made it 13 to 14. Even though we went down and scored and made the game 21 to 13, they still had momentum because they were able to score a touchdown on their previous possession, that was all they needed.

Oklahoma State defeated West Virginia 41-24, turning a 14-13 halftime deficit into a 17-point victory. The Cowboys scored 28 second-half points and finished with 609 total yards.

So let's grade every position group. Not just based on the final score. Let's talk football.

Michael Hawkins Jr. gave us two very different performances Saturday night. With his legs, he was electric. Through the air, this was easily his most difficult game of the season. He finished with 132 passing yards, completing 10 of 22 attempts with an interception. He was also sacked four times. You cannot finish with less than a 50% completion percentage and get higher than a B with me.

But he rushed for 102 yards and three touchdowns. That's the dilemma with Hawkins. You can see the playmaking ability. You can see why we can be dangerous with him at quarterback.

Big 12 defenses are eventually going to force him to win football games with his arm. Oklahoma State did a good job disrupting his rhythm, and West Virginia became increasingly dependent on the running game.

According to PFF's postgame grades, Hawkins received a 72.2 overall grade, which was actually one of the better offensive grades for WVU.

This position group doesn't need much explanation.

29 carries. 193 yards. 6.7 yards per carry.

That's a legitimate running-back performance. And it wasn't just Cook. We finished with 334 rushing yards as a team, with Hawkins adding another 102. We averaged roughly 6.3 yards per carry. The running game gave West Virginia a chance to win this football game.

In fact, I'm comfortable saying this, the running backs were not the reason West Virginia lost. PFF gave Cam Cook a 75.8 grade and Amari Latimer a 76.3.

This is where things get difficult. We had only 132 passing yards. DJ Epps led the Mountaineers with 39 receiving yards. That's not enough production from the receiver room.

Now, we have to be fair. The passing game wasn't simply a case of receivers failing to get open. Oklahoma State's defensive pressure and West Virginia's offensive approach both played a role.

But when the running game is producing 334 yards, somebody eventually has to make a defense pay for loading the box. That didn't happen consistently. And that's going to become a problem if opposing defenses decide they can force West Virginia to throw.

The tight ends weren't a major factor in the passing game. We needed another reliable way to attack the middle of the field, particularly when Oklahoma State began focusing on the run.

The position group didn't provide enough production to change the complexion of the game. This wasn't necessarily a catastrophic performance. It was simply too quiet.

This is probably the most complicated position group to grade. On one hand, West Virginia rushed for 334 yards. That's phenomenal. On the other hand, Michael Hawkins was sacked four times.

Oklahoma State also generated significant pressure.

PFF's individual grades tell an interesting story. Right tackle Carsten Casady received a 64.8 overall grade but was credited with seven pressures allowed. True freshman Kevin Brown received a 59.1 grade and allowed four pressures, including two sacks.

So I'm not going to give the offensive line an A simply because the rushing numbers were excellent. The run blocking was good. The pass protection wasn't good enough.

The defensive line had a difficult night. Oklahoma State ran for 220 yards and threw for 389. That means the front wasn't consistently controlling either phase. There were moments when the defensive line created disruption, but not nearly enough of it.

And perhaps most importantly, Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker wasn't sacked. That's a major problem when you're facing a quarterback who ultimately throws for 389 yards and three touchdowns. Now, I know we're talking a lot about the passing game, but every time Oklahoma State ran the ball to their left, it was for 6+ yards at least, we couldn't even stop them in the running game.

PFF's highest defensive-line grades were Corey McIntyre Jr. at 67.7 and Zeke Durham-Campbell at 67.1.

The edge rushers didn't generate enough pressure.

That's particularly concerning because West Virginia needed to make Mestemaker uncomfortable. Instead, he was allowed to settle into the game.

Rich Rodriguez himself pointed to the lack of pressure afterward, saying West Virginia didn't get enough pressure on Mestemaker and that the quarterback was able to get comfortable. Against a quarterback who ultimately completed 20 of 27 passes for 389 yards, that is a recipe for trouble.

There were some individual positives, but collectively this group needed to be better. Isaiah Patterson posted the highest PFF grade among WVU linebackers at 70.7. But the group struggled to consistently affect the game, particularly as Oklahoma State began generating explosive plays. SECONDARY — F

This was the position group that ultimately broke the game open.

Oklahoma State threw for 389 yards. Wyatt Young caught eight passes for 192 yards. before this game, we was given up big pass place because we couldn't keep containment, and the quarterback was scrambling, causing the secondary to collapse. This game, the quarterback had a clean pocket and didn't need to scramble, and we still gave up the yardage. Our defense has a major problem.

The Cowboys repeatedly found opportunities downfield, and seven of their 12 plays of 20 yards or more came in the second half. Four of those second-half explosive plays were passes of at least 40 yards. That's unacceptable defensive production. And this wasn't simply one player having a bad night.

PFF's postgame grades show problems throughout the secondary. Nick Taylor allowed four catches on four targets for 69 yards, while Andrew Powdrell surrendered three catches on three targets for 116 yards.

Special teams wasn't the reason West Virginia lost this game. There wasn't a major special-teams collapse that explains the 41-24 final score. This group did its job reasonably well.

This one deserves some nuance. I don't think West Virginia walked into this game unprepared. The Mountaineers led 14-13 at halftime and 24-21 in the third quarter. The game plan clearly understood where WVU had an advantage: the ground game.

The problem was what happened after Oklahoma State adjusted. The Cowboys scored 28 second-half points. West Virginia couldn't find an answer. That's where the coaching grade comes down. You don't have to abandon the running game. But you have to find ways to make the defense respect the passing game. And defensively, you have to find a way to stop the explosive plays.

Here's my biggest takeaway from this game: West Virginia wasn't incapable of beating Oklahoma State. That's what makes this loss frustrating. The Mountaineers had a running game capable of controlling the game.

We had a quarterback who could make plays with his legs. We had a lead. We had the home crowd. We had opportunities. But Oklahoma State made the explosive plays that West Virginia couldn't prevent.

That's how you lose a football game even when your own offense rushes for 334 yards.

The good news? I don't think the identity of this team is broken. The running game is legitimate. Cam Cook is legitimate. Hawkins has legitimate playmaking ability, but we have to become more balanced offensively and significantly better defensively. Because the Big 12 isn't going to get easier. The Mountaineers are now 3-1 overall and 0-1 in conference play.

And that's where the conversation changes. We're not grading preseason expectations anymore. We're grading what is actually happening on the field. An after Oklahoma State, here's my report card:

QB — C+ RB — A WR — D+ TE — C- OL — C DL — C- EDGE — D LB — C- DB — F Special Teams — B Coaching — C

The Mountaineers can run the football. Now they have to prove they can stop somebody. Because 334 rushing yards should be enough to win a football game. When it isn't, you know exactly where you need to start looking.

articles.title: Irish football body launches review over alleged racist ‘monkey chants’ after UEFA refuses to investigate Ireland-Israel clash
articles.summary: The Football Association of Ireland is conducting a review after allegations of racist chanting directed at forward Adam Idah during the Nations League match against Israel. Amid controversies, UEFA declines to investigate due to procedural issues.
articles.body: The Football Association of Ireland is reviewing footage and audio recordings after an allegation that Irish forward Adam Idah was subjected to racist chanting during Ireland’s 3–0 Nations League win over Israel. The claim emerged after midfielder Jayson Molumby alerted match officials during the game, while UEFA has told the FAI that its own disciplinary process cannot begin because the required reporting procedure was not followed.FAI review allegations after Molumby raises concern during matchThe allegation centres on events during Ireland’s 3–0 victory over Israel at the Nagyerdei Stadium in Debrecen, Hungary, on Sunday.Idah, who scored Ireland’s second goal, is reported to have been targeted by chants from sections of the Israeli support. The 25-year-old, who was born to a Nigerian father and an Irish mother, was said to be unaware of the alleged abuse while the match was taking place.According to The Irish Times, Molumby heard what he believed were racist chants aimed at Idah before half-time. The Ireland midfielder approached referee Harm Osmers and fourth official Florian Exner and asked them to “listen”, pointing towards the stands.The officials did not hear chanting that they considered racist and the incident was not formally reported on the pitch as a racial-abuse allegation.A UEFA match delegate later informed the FAI that the matter could not be investigated through UEFA's disciplinary process because the correct protocol had not been followed. Molumby had not explicitly identified the chanting as racist when speaking to the officials, while the officials themselves had not heard the alleged abuse.The FAI has since decided to conduct its own review. The association is examining available video and audio footage to establish what was said in the stands and whether Idah was subjected to racist abuse.Al Jazeera has reported that videos circulating on social media appear to show Israeli supporters directing “monkey chants” towards Idah during the match.Israeli supporters also filmed military chants after the defeatThe allegations surrounding Idah emerged alongside another incident involving supporters in the Israeli section of the stadium.Youseph Haddad, who is described in the reporting as a member of an Israeli right-wing party and a candidate for the country's upcoming parliamentary elections, filmed himself among supporters during the match and posted footage on social media.The video showed supporters chanting about the Israeli military as their team fell to a 3–0 defeat.“Yes, we lose in football, but where we don’t lose, the IDF [Israeli Defence Force]. We always win,” Haddad said in the video.“So maybe the football Irish team beat us on the football field, but they will never, ever break the Israeli spirit.”It is not clear whether the chants about the Israeli military would fall within UEFA's rules on spectator behaviour. UEFA's disciplinary regulations allow sanctions ranging from fines to stadium closures and restrictions on away supporters when national associations are found responsible for prohibited spectator conduct, but such penalties require a disciplinary process.The match itself had already attracted significant attention before kick-off because of political pressure surrounding Ireland's decision to fulfil its Nations League fixtures against Israel.The FAI had previously asked UEFA whether Ireland and Israel could be kept apart in future competition draws. UEFA rejected that request, saying such decisions were not based on public sentiment and noting that the countries had never been in direct conflict.Ireland's players had already taken several symbolic actionsThe events in Debrecen came after days of internal discussions within the Ireland squad over whether the fixture should be played.Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad after speaking with his teammates and explaining that he did not feel he could participate in the matches against Israel.“I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of character and principle. Therefore, I feel it would be wrong to participate in the upcoming fixtures against Israel,” Bazunu said.Ireland ultimately went ahead with the match after discussions between the players and the FAI. The decision came after months of pressure from campaigners calling for the fixtures to be boycotted in response to Israel's war in Gaza.On the pitch, Ireland's players wore black armbands, with FAI chief executive David Courell saying they were worn in recognition of “all lives lost” in the conflict. The players also bowed their heads during Israel's national anthem and did not shake hands with their opponents before kick-off.Ireland captain Dara O'Shea did not shake hands with Israel captain Dor Peretz, while reports also said O'Shea had pledged to donate his match earnings to humanitarian aid for Gaza.The match itself remained one-sided. Troy Parrott opened the scoring, Idah added the second and Jack Moylan completed the 3–0 victory.Jake O'Brien and Manor Solomon also clashed during the matchThe political tension surrounding the fixture spilled into an on-field exchange involving Ireland defender Jake O'Brien and Israel winger Manor Solomon.Reports said the two players became involved in an angry confrontation during the match, with O'Brien allegedly telling Solomon: “Shame on you for what you’re doing in Gaza. You deserve to lose.”Solomon responded: “Come out, be a man. Don’t talk behind a wall. It’s a shame the game wasn’t in Israel, you would understand what the best country in the world is.”Speaking after the match, Solomon declined to repeat what had been said during the confrontation but made clear that the relationship between the two sides had become hostile.“They said nonsense during the game, I don’t want to comment on them,” Solomon said.He further added that he held back from saying more because of the possibility of suspension.“If I say what I think about them I’ll probably be banned for a few games so I don’t want to say, of course they hate us and we don’t like them.”Solomon also looked ahead to the return fixture.“I’m already looking forward to the next game against them, it’s going to be completely different.”He later added: “They (the Irish players) don’t interest me. We have a country ten times better than theirs, stronger, an amazing country with amazing people.”“We are proud to wear the team shirt and to be Israelis. We are proud of our state and of our soldiers.”“They can play all their tricks. We are Israelis and love the country. And that will always be the case.”Ireland's next Nations League match is against Austria at the Aviva Stadium on October 1, while Israel will host Kosovo on the same day.The return fixture between Ireland and Israel is scheduled for October 4 at the TSC Arena in Bačka Topola, Serbia. articles.standfirst: El extremo del Bayern entró en la segunda mitad y desatascó el partido en el tramo final
articles.summary: El extremo del Bayern entró en la segunda mitad y desatascó el partido en el tramo final
articles.body: Olise dio los tres puntos a Francia en un partido marcado por la revolución de Zidane. El técnico francés, obligado a encontrar un sustituto para Mbappé, convirtió su casting en una rotación masiva y solo Maignan y Lacroix repitieron respecto al duelo ante Turquía. Enfrente aparecía una nueva Bélgica, con van Bommel al frente y todavía lejos de aquella generación dorada, aunque con supervivientes como De Bruyne o Tielemans. Los 'Diablos Rojos' también llegaban con una victoria bajo el brazo, cosechada ante una Italia muy pobre. Pero el rival que tenían delante era muy diferente. Ante las suplencias de Olise y Dembélé, fue Doué quien tomó el mando del ataque galo. En un once en el que debutaban hasta tres jugadores (Jacquet, Diouf y Da Cunha), además de Lepaul, que apenas había tenido minutos contra los turcos, Francia salió decidida a hacerse con el balón, con Camavinga como timonel. En el 11’ llegó la primera gran ocasión francesa. Doué se marcó un vals ante la defensa belga, caracoleando con la calidad que ya acostumbra hasta encontrar el espacio para sacar el disparo, que terminó estrellándose en el larguero. Apenas cinco minutos después, Lepaul se giró con un gran movimiento para rematar un centro del extremo del PSG, aunque sin encontrar portería. La réplica local llegó en el 17’. De Bruyne encontró a De Ketelaere, pero el atacante no consiguió conectar con el balón cuando ya tenía a Maignan vencido. Los galos volvieron a rozar el gol en el 26’, después de una triple ocasión que terminó con Lavia sacando bajo palos el disparo de Kalulu. El partido se fue igualando y los de 'Zizou' perdieron protagonismo con el paso de los minutos. De Bruyne estuvo cerca de aprovecharlo en el 36’, cuando buscó la escuadra con un disparo que se marchó por muy poco. Francia pisó el acelerador tras el descanso y acumuló ocasiones en apenas cinco minutos. En el 51’, Doué volvió a probar desde lejos, aunque su disparo se marchó fuera. Dos minutos después, Da Cunha estrelló el balón en el palo con otro lanzamiento desde la distancia. Y en el 56’, Doué obligó a Lammens a intervenir para evitar el gol. En el rechace, Lepaul no consiguió dirigir el balón hacia la portería. Bélgica sufría. Pero los 'Diablos Rojos' también tenían algo que decir. En el 72’, Lukebakio obligó a intervenir a Maignan con un disparo que puso de nuevo a prueba al meta francés. Zidane buscó entonces más pólvora dando entrada a Dembélé, Olise y Cherki. El partido transcurría tranquilo, camino del tramo final, hasta que Olise se inventó una gran diagonal, recorriendo más de medio campo antes de batir a Lammens y darle la victoria a Francia. El tanto desató la locura en el banquillo galo y Zidane celebró de forma efusiva su segundo triunfo como seleccionador.

articles.title: De Astarloa a Ballan, McNulty irrumpe en la galería de campeones inesperados
articles.standfirst: Su ataque a 32 kilómetros de meta en Montreal le da el arcoíris y lo sitúa junto a Vainsteins, Astarloa, Ballan o Pedersen
articles.summary: Su ataque a 32 kilómetros de meta en Montreal le da el arcoíris y lo sitúa junto a Vainsteins, Astarloa, Ballan o Pedersen
articles.body: El Mundial es una carrera de un solo día, sin segunda oportunidad. Un circuito, equipos nacionales que deben coordinarse sin pinganillos y un puñado de movimientos capaces de desmontar cualquier quiniela. Brandon McNulty lo ha vuelto a demostrar en Montreal: el estadounidense atacó a 32 kilómetros de la línea, se fue en solitario y transformó un ataque lejano en el maillot de campeón del mundo. Su triunfo interrumpe la racha de los últimos años, dominada por Tadej Pogacar (ausente esta vez por su caída en La Vuelta), Remco Evenepoel, Mathieu Van der Poel o Julian Alaphilippe, retirado tras el último Tour. McNulty se suma así a una nómina que el ciclismo engrosa desde hace décadas: la de quienes llegaron al Mundial sin los focos encima y se fueron con el arcoíris puesto. Para encontrar los primeros ejemplos del siglo hay que retroceder hasta Plouay 2000. Óscar Freire, que ya había ganado por sorpresa en Verona, partía como gran favorito, pero Roman Vainsteins se lo arrebató en el esprint y el español vio escaparse el título cuando parecía suyo. En 2003 fue Canadá la que albergó otra sorpresa. En Hamilton, Igor Astarloa lanzó un ataque contundente en los últimos kilómetros y, mientras los favoritos se vigilaban, se marchó en solitario. Alejandro Valverde completó el doblete español con la plata, por delante de veteranos como Peter Van Petegem, Paolo Bettini, Erik Zabel o Tom Boonen. Un año más tarde, Freire se cobraría su tercer arcoíris. En Varese 2008 los ojos italianos apuntaban a Paolo Bettini, que aspiraba a un tercer título seguido. Fue Alessandro Ballan quien demarró en la última vuelta, ganó unos metros y no volvió a ser alcanzado. Italia consiguió el oro por un camino distinto al previsto. Doce meses después, Mendrisio volvió a apartarse del guion: Suiza confiaba en Fabian Cancellara sobre un trazado durísimo, pero el movimiento decisivo lo firmó Cadel Evans. El australiano, con currículum en las grandes vueltas, sumó aquel arcoíris a una trayectoria que dos años después incluiría el Tour de Francia. En 2010, en Geelong, sobre un recorrido menos selectivo, Thor Hushovd resolvió la prueba mientras Freire buscaba su cuarto título y Philippe Gilbert empezaba a dominar las clásicas. Florencia 2013 dejó una de las estampas más amargas para el ciclismo español. Purito Rodríguez y Alejandro Valverde se jugaron el título con Rui Costa en una situación de dos contra uno que acabó favoreciendo al portugués. Costa dio caza a Purito y ganó el arcoíris, mientras Rodríguez y Valverde se conformaron con la plata y el bronce. Entre los aspirantes de aquel día también estaban Philippe Gilbert, Fabian Cancellara o Cadel Evans. Los dos españoles en el podio dieron la medida de lo que se perdió. Ponferrada 2014 volvió a descolocar los pronósticos. Michal Kwiatkowski venía de una temporada sobresaliente: Trofeo Serra de Tramuntana, Volta ao Algarve y Strade Bianche en su palmarés, segundo en la Vuelta al País Vasco y en la Vuelta a Gran Bretaña, y tercero en la Flecha Valona y en Lieja-Bastoña-Lieja. Aun así, la atención estaba puesta en otros. El polaco atacó en el tramo final, ganó unos metros y llegó solo a meta, por delante del grupo de favoritos. Valverde fue bronce, y Gilbert, Van Avermaet o Cancellara se quedaron sin el maillot en el último Mundial disputado en España hasta ahora. Yorkshire 2019 recuperó la tradición de los campeones improbables. Mads Pedersen no era un desconocido (había sido segundo en el Tour de Flandes 2018 y sumaba victorias en carreras menores), pero no figuraba entre los candidatos principales, con Peter Sagan, Alejandro Valverde, Julian Alaphilippe, Mathieu Van der Poel, Greg Van Avermaet o Philippe Gilbert por delante en las apuestas. Van der Poel llegó a tirar del grupo antes de desfondarse, y Pedersen aguantó hasta disputar el título en un esprint agónico en el que batió a Matteo Trentin y Stefan Küng, bajo unas condiciones climáticas extremas. Vinieron después los años de Alaphilippe, Evenepoel, Van der Poel y Pogacar, una sucesión de estrellas que hizo pensar que el Mundial era siempre cosa de los grandes nombres. Montreal ha mostrado lo contrario. McNulty atacó con 32 kilómetros por delante, abrió hueco con sus perseguidores y remató en solitario. Cruzó la meta como campeón del mundo y se sumó a una lista que ya integraban Vainsteins, Astarloa, Ballan, Evans, Hushovd, Rui Costa, Kwiatkowski y Pedersen.

articles.title: Miami OC Calls Out SEC, Blasts 'Ridiculous' CFB Preseason Rankings in New Video
articles.summary: Miami is No. 4 in the most recent Associated Press Top 25 poll, but its schedule and lack of ranked opponents figure to remain a talking point throughout the season.
articles.body:
Miami is No. 4 in the most recent Associated Press Top 25 poll, but its schedule and lack of ranked opponents figure to remain a talking point throughout the season.

With that as the backdrop, Hurricanes offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson is pushing back at the idea of having preseason rankings in the first place that can heavily impact how teams are seen and ranked later in the season. He also isn't a fan of all the love the SEC receives in those rankings.

"First of all, there should be no such thing as preseason rankings," Dawson told reporters . "That's the most ridiculous thing on the planet. That is the stupidest thing, because people weigh those things way heavier than they should.

"You shouldn't have a ranking until October. How do you know? (Texas) A&M was ranked in the top-five, but how does that look right now? If anything, it isn't predictable for the future, it's the past. Go look at the top-10 last year. I did. Five of them weren't even in the (end of season) Top 25."

Texas A&M is no longer ranked after losing to Kentucky and LSU by a combined 39 points in back-to-back weeks, but there are plenty of SEC teams rounding out the Top 25 with teams such as Kentucky and Missouri sneaking into the Nos. 24 and 25 spots.

Tennessee is also No. 17 despite extended struggles, along with Missouri, when it comes to beating even mediocre teams:

It seems like Dawson is aware of the SEC love, some of it unearned, from the voters.

"So we sit here and look at schedules, and obviously everything is SEC, SEC. Well look … they have all of their teams in the Top 25," he said. "Guess what. Good for you. At the end of the year, half of them won't be in the top 30. That's just the way it is. We can't sit here and say, 'hey, we play X number of Top-25 teams.' We don't know that. We'll count those chips up at the end of the year."

Miami did plenty of counting at the end of last season when it defeated two SEC teams in Texas A&M and Ole Miss in the College Football Playoff on the way to the national championship game, where it lost to Indiana.

Indiana's win gave the Big Ten three straight titles and continued the SEC's recent CFP issues:

At this point, the Hurricanes have just one team on their entire schedule this season that is ranked. That opponent is No. 3 Notre Dame, who they will face in a highly anticipated showdown on Nov. 7.

The schedule will be a talking point, although the CFP selection committee's rankings are the ones that will ultimately matter and not the AP poll.

Whether that committee is influenced by preseason rankings and so many SEC teams being ranked remains to be seen, but Dawson is doing his best to fight back at the notion the teams in that conference are better than others because of where they started the season in the poll.

articles.title: Northern Ireland 0-0 Hungary: Michael O'Neill's side left frustrated by goalless draw in Belfast
articles.summary: Match report as Northern Ireland drew 0-0 with Hungary in the Nations League; Patrick Kelly went close twice before Isaac Price was denied by Balazs Toth late on; Northern Ireland were the better side but could not find a breakthrough
articles.body:
Patrick Kelly twice went close in the first half and Isaac Price was denied by Balazs Toth late on, but Northern Ireland could not find a goal which would have made it a perfect start to the campaign in Group B2 of the Nations League.

They looked the better side against higher-ranked opposition who struggled to create chances until the latter stages of a night when Liverpool star Dominik Szoboszlai's most notable contribution was to charge up the Windsor Park crowd.

There were nervous moments in the closing stages as Ruairi McConville made a key block from Willi Orban and Pierce Charles saved from Alex Toth to preserve his fifth clean sheet in seven competitive appearances for Northern Ireland.

It means Michael O'Neill's side have lost only one of their last 10 games in Belfast, and they looked resolute again with Hungary managing only one shot on target.

The major frustration for O'Neill will be the number of yellow cards shown by referee Ricardo De Burgos, with four Northern Ireland players - Shea Charles, Jamie Donley, Isaac Price and Ethan Galbraith - going in the book along with the manager himself.

Coming off the back of Friday's last-gasp 1-0 win in Tbilisi and enjoying the roar of a Windsor Park crowd for the first time in 315 days, Northern Ireland were quick to get at Hungary with a strong press, picking off hurried passes from the visiting defence.

That led to chances for the busy Galbraith and Price early on before Trai Hume sent a shot from the edge of the area narrowly wide.

Northern Ireland's best two chances of the first half both came for Kelly. Just after the half-hour mark, Price slipped it through and the Barnsley midfielder tried to chip Blackburn's Balazs Toth but could not get enough height on the shot with the goal gaping.

Then Tom Atcheson flicked on a Ciaron Brown long throw, and although Shea Charles could not reach the ball as he tussled with Milos Kerkez, it fell for an off-balance Kelly who looped it up on to the top of the crossbar.

Hungary were not enjoying Northern Ireland's physical approach as they struggled to threaten and tempers began to fray.

After Donley became the third home player to be booked O'Neill also saw yellow for his protests and the half ended in confrontation after Charles left Daniel Lukacs in a heap challenging for a high ball.

Hungary began to get forward more after the break. Schafer sent a snapshot wide inside the box, then missed the target from long range after a short free-kick before Donat Barany headed over from a corner.

Northern Ireland were struggling to get forward as they had in the first half, but from a free-kick pumped into the box Price spun away from Kerkez before seeing his shot saved at the near post.

At the other end, McConville threw himself in front of a close-range strike from Orban and Charles repelled a powerful strike from Bournemouth's Alex Toth as time ticked down.

articles.title: Algo ha pasado en el Balón de Oro: espectacular remontada de Lamine
articles.standfirst: Todas las predicciones apuntaban a Kane... pero ahora el español es el favorito para llevárselo
articles.summary: Todas las predicciones apuntaban a Kane... pero ahora el español es el favorito para llevárselo
articles.body: Ya se han cerrado las votaciones para el Balón de Oro. Las elecciones para seleccionar al mejor futbolista del año acaban de terminar, por lo que ya está decidido quién levantará el galardón el próximo 26 de octubre. Sólo falta leer y recontar los votos. Son varios los pretendientes para recibir el premio con argumentos individuales y colectivos. Aunque en las últimas horas ha habido una gran remontada en las candidaturas. Un subidón que invita a pensar en un vuelco sobre la bocina. Desde que acabó el Mundial, Harry Kane apuntaba a convertirse en Balón de Oro. Muchas páginas de predicciones y casas de apuestas daban como favorito al inglés. Pero en la recta final hay una corriente a favor de Lamine Yamal para que gane el trofeo. Y en las últimas horas, el futbolista del Barça ha experimentado una gran remontada. Hace apenas una semana, la cuota de que el jugador del Bayern fuese nombrado mejor jugador del año estaba a 1.65, mientras que la de Lamine era más del doble, 3.75. Unos días después, incluso las cuotas eran más bajas, 1.62 frente a los 3.25 del español, unas cuotas que dejaban como gran favorito a Kane. Sin embargo, la probabilidad ha dado un giro total. Este lunes, a las doce de la noche, se cerraba la votación para elegir al galardón y la situación no puede estar más apretada. Según las casas de predicciones, el domingo por la noche Kane tenía un 56%de opciones de hacerse con el galardón y Lamine un 28%. Pero tras apenas unas horas, el '10' del Barça se ha elevado al primer puesto con un 45% de probabilidades de ganar el premio frente al 42% del inglés. Detrás de este giro de los acontecimientos no sabemos qué motivo puede haber. Una de las razones puede ser la existencia de un gran inversor, que haya ingresado grandes cantidades de dinero y quiera obtener beneficio económico. También es probable que las filtraciones no oficiales hayan llevado a algunos a creer que el premio ya estaba otorgado y quieran aprovecharlo. Otra de las razones puede ser la primera jornada de la Nations League. España venció a Inglaterra y, aunque ambos marcaron (Harry con la ayuda de Cucurella), la victoria puede explicar que el español haya adelantado al inglés. Además Kane falló un penalti que hubiese sido el 3-1. Por ello, puede que la figura de Lamine haya crecido desde entonces. Este giro en las cuotas va de la mano con los resultados de la gran encuesta realizada por MARCA, en la que Lamine Yamal es el gran favorito para hacerse con el Balón de Oro el próximo 26 de octubre en una votación con casi 350.000 participaciones. Sin embargo, en esta predicción, Harry Kane baja hasta la cuarta posición, teniendo por delante a Kylian Mbappé, Bota de Oro de Champions y Mundial; y Fabián Ruiz, ganador de Champions y Mundial. Las cuotas ya han decidido quién será el ganador, aunque habrá que esperar hasta el día de la gala para ver si coinciden o no con el mejor futbolista el año.

articles.title: Dylan Stewart Suspended for Punching Alabama Player, Arguing with South Carolina Coach
articles.summary: South Carolina star edge rusher Dylan Stewart has been suspended for one game after punching an Alabama player and arguing with coaches during Saturday's 49-18 loss.
articles.body:
South Carolina star edge rusher Dylan Stewart has been suspended for one game after punching an Alabama player and arguing with coaches during Saturday's 49-18 loss.

"Dylan Stewart's egregious contact reflects behavior that is unacceptable and not aligned with the standards of the Southeastern Conference," SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said in a statement . "Such action against an opponent carries a serious risk of injury and has no place in our conference competition. This suspension is appropriate, and any future misconduct by Dylan Stewart will result in more severe disciplinary action."

That news came one day after Gamecocks head coach Shane Beamer told reporters on Sunday that Stewart was suspended indefinitely.

"I'll make the decision on what his future looks like beyond this week here in the next day or so. Still having some meetings and talking with him, but he won't play his week versus Kentucky. There's a standard of how we do things in our program and that was not it last night," Beamer told reporters . "It's beyond the punch. The punch is unacceptable. He's not the first person to ever throw a punch in the football game and he won't be the last. But it's some of the other stuff that isn't how we do things in this program. Accountability is a core value in this program and we are all accountable to the standard, so we'll see what that looks like here going forward."

Beamer didn't comment on the other specific things that led to the decision when asked by reporters, but Stewart did not appear to appreciate being pulled from the game at one point. On another occasion he took his time getting off the field, much to the chagrin of Beamer.

"It gets heated down there. Dylan and a coach—players and coaches—there's intense conversations and things that happen during games," Beamer noted. "And you know that you're in a competitive hostile environment. ... We're going to hold guys accountable for things. That's what we're doing here. That's what we do with all of our players. Dylan and South Carolina are not the first place that have had interactions that get heated on the sideline. It's a competitive environment and I've seen a lot of them over the years, whether it be at Georgia or Tennessee or Oklahoma or wherever else I've coached over the years."

The entire situation could have a major impact on Stewart's draft stock. Coming into the season, the B/R NFL Scouting Department projected him as a potential top-10 pick at the 2027 NFL draft.

Stewart, a junior, recorded 11 sacks through his first two seasons. He hasn't posted a sack through two games this season, however, and has just one tackle.

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa president indicates there could a greater cash pledge to members
articles.summary: Fifa president Gianni Infantino indicates more money could be distributed to the governing body's members from its cash reserves.
articles.body:
Gianni Infantino has indicated a greater amount of money could be distributed to Fifa members from its estimated £4.4bn cash reserves.

In a letter seen by BBC Sport, and sent to the governing body's six continental confederations on Monday, Fifa president Infantino said he would support "the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered".

Infantino has come under increasing pressure over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, which proposed selling stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors, sparking a major backlash.

His letter comes after Uefa and Concacaf - the confederations for Europe and North America, Central America and the Caribbean - demanded Fifa pays $10m (£7.5m) to all 211 members from its reserves.

The proposal will be considered by the Fifa Council when they meet on 15 October.

"I will not prejudge the amount," Infantino said in the letter.

"A single figure can begin the discussion, but it cannot complete a global policy."

Infantino issued his latest defence of the failed proposal to sell a slice of the World Cup commercial rights that brought calls for his resignation, again claiming it had been intended to generate additional money for the game.

"The recent commercial proposal, now withdrawn, was intended to enable Fifa to invest more in football," wrote the Swiss-Italian.

Earlier this month, Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt, a Fifa vice-president, told Infantino to release all documents relating to his controversial plan, and called for an independent review of FFE.

Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

articles.title: Bill Belichick Addresses UNC Investigation, Says Team Will 'Do Everything the Right Way'
articles.summary: Following an investigation into the culture of North Carolina's football program, Tar Heels head coach Bill Belichick addressed the investigation's findings and resolution.
articles.body:
Following an investigation into the culture of North Carolina's football program, Tar Heels head coach Bill Belichick addressed the investigation's findings and resolution.

"We have a plan in place to continue to make this, our workplace, function at a high standard and do everything the right way," Belichick said, per The Athletic's Brendan Marks .

The investigation found that "certain actions demonstrated a disregard for Carolina's values and standards of conduct." Belichick said that he and the leaders of the program will continue to meet with the outside counsel that conducted the investigation.

"That's our goal, to do things the right way, and be productive and consistent doing them," Belichick said. "In areas that we can improve in, we should … do that. All that was done by the outside counsel and the people that were part of that, and so we'll meet with them — and have met with them — to finalize (that)."

The investigation included allegations of drug use and inappropriate relationships, though the university said the actions were "isolated" and "not a systematic failure."

Belichick said that he "tried to do" what investigators asked and that he "cooperated with them the best I could."

UNC's football general manager, Michael Lombardi, was placed on administrative leave by the school over the summer after a human resources complaint filed by a former UNC front office employee. That led to a larger investigation of the program, and Lombardi later resigned from his position.

Amid the investigation, Belichick's son and the team's defensive coordinator, Steve Belichick, also resigned .

North Carolina, which is in its second season under Belichick, started the season 2-0 with wins over TCU and ETSU before a 28-20 loss against Clemson. After a bye week on Saturday, the Tar Heels will face No. 3 Notre Dame on Saturday.

articles.title: Northern Ireland 0-0 Hungary: Michael O'Neill 'positive' as NI maintain unbeaten start
articles.summary: Michael O'Neill says he is "positive" as Northern Ireland maintain their unbeaten start in the Nations League with a goalless draw with Hungary.
articles.body:
After 315 days away from Windsor Park, Northern Ireland's goalless draw with Hungary on their homecoming did not have the same drama as the late win over Georgia on Friday night.

But that suited Northern Ireland just fine.

On their return to League B in the Nations League, they sit joint-top with Ukraine with four points from their opening two matches.

It's a result that left manager Michael O'Neill feeling "positive" at the halfway point of the four-game window.

"We played a very good side, I thought we were more than a match for the opposition," said O'Neill on Hungary, who lost their opener 1-0 to Ukraine on Friday.

"It's another clean sheet for us, which is positive, but we just couldn't find maybe enough to create that clear-cut chance that we'd win the game."

Northern Ireland top group despite Hungary stalemate

Chances were at a premium at Windsor Park as both defences came out on top.

Patrick Kelly hit the crossbar in the first half for Northern Ireland, and Isaac Price had an effort beaten away by Balazs Toth.

After Dan Ballard controversially conceded a penalty in Georgia, Shea Charles also had a penalty appeal waved away in the lead-up to the Kelly chance for a similar incident.

While O'Neill said he had yet to see it back, he did quip that "the referee never seems to make the walk for us to the side of the pitch. It never seems to happen for us."

The threat of Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai was largely nullified throughout the game as Hungary, like Northern Ireland, struggled to create any clear-cut chances.

The only save that Pierce Charles had to make in goal was when a lethargic clearance led to Alex Toth shooting towards goal in the closing stages, but the QPR stopper was otherwise untroubled.

After a 5,000-mile trip from Georgia in their opening game, Northern Ireland had to quickly reset and O'Neill admitted he saw "two tired teams" at the end of the game.

"I think our preparation, our first game in terms of being away from home and everything, was more difficult.

"I felt like Hungary got a little bit stronger towards the end."

One point that did irk O'Neill was perceived play acting from some of the visiting players.

Ethan Galbraith, captain Shea Charles, Jamie Donley and Isaac Price were all booked by Spanish referee Ricardo de Burgos, and O'Neill felt the visitors played their part in a stop-start game.

"I was disappointed with some of the yellow cards that were given, and I was disappointed with some of the Hungarian players' behaviour on the pitch, holding their face and screaming," O'Neill said.

"Really, there was no need for that. It was an honest, competitive game. We didn't need the nature of the simulation or the antics.

"We want that away and out of the game. That's why the referee has to speed the game up."

Northern Ireland are back on the road in their third game of the quadruple-header when they face Ukraine in Slovakia on Friday.

It will be another difficult test for a youthful Northern Ireland side, but for now O'Neill is pleased with what he described as a "great start".

"It's a very good start in a very, very competitive group," he added.

"If you look at the results so far, you can see that. The teams seem very well matched."

articles.title: Tranquilidad y optimismo con la final del Mundial 2030
articles.standfirst: La RFEF sigue trabajando para traer la final a España cuando se abre la vía de un posible partido inaugural en Marruecos.
articles.summary: La RFEF sigue trabajando para traer la final a España cuando se abre la vía de un posible partido inaugural en Marruecos.
articles.body: Ningún actor del mundo del fútbol lo duda (excepto Marruecos): España debe ser la sede de la final del Mundial 2030. Por lo deportivo: es la reciente campeona del mundo y vive la época más dorada de su historia en todas sus categorías y secciones. Y por lo lo logístico: es la organizadora principal del Mundial 2030 y cuenta con el apoyo de Portugal, el socio más directo e importante de la candidatura. A partir de aquí se abren distintos escenarios. La candidatura ibérica (España y Portugal) es potente y sólida desde el primer momento. Un paso fugaz de Ucrania y la llegada de Argentina, Paraguay y Uruguay como homenaje al centenario tampoco fueron un problema, pero Marruecos siempre quiso más. El máximo representante de la candidatura marroquí, Fouzi Lekjaa, aprieta. Y lo hace consciente de sus puntos fuertes: están construyendo un estadio con capacidad para 115.000 espectadores, trabajan para convencer a Infantino convirtiendo su país en un hogar para la FIFA y tienen claro hacia dónde apuntar: Casablanca. Mientras tanto, en España, el mensaje es el de tranquilidad y optimismo. La Real Federación Española de Fútbol, con su presidente a la cabeza, trabaja en una final en nuestro país, pero sigue sin decidir -o expresar públicamente- si será Madrid o Barcelona. "Tiene que ser en España, no hay otra opción", repite constantemente Rafael Louzán. "España no puede tener dudas en todo esto, somos potencia y líderes mundiales en todo. Acaban de ganar las chicas del sub-20 ayer y mañana vamos a intentar dar otra alegría a España. Aunque la alegría más importante será jugar la final en España", explicó el presidente en 'Otra Ronda' este lunes. Marruecos no lo pondrá fácil. La negociación es tosca porque el país africano está como loco por albergar el gran evento del 2030, pero la Federación no tiene pensado reblar a sus intereses. Pese a que desde dentro se lamenta que garantizar la final en España no fuese un punto de partida claro en el acuerdo, el equipo de la candidatura trabaja para que el partido se quede en nuestro país. Una opción que aparece en el horizonte es que el partido inaugural se dispute en Marruecos y la final en España. Esto dejaría en el aire el papel de los tres países sudamericanos, pero podría ser un escenario interesante para España. Con las elecciones de la FIFA a la vuelta de la esquina y el determinante papel de la confederación europea en el aire, el futuro de la final del 2030 (y de Infantino) sigue sin esclarecerse, aunque España trabaja en la sombra para poner la guinda a su Mundial.

articles.summary: College Football can be odd. The Nebraska Cornhuskers are undefeated following the walloping they gave to the Michigan State Spartans Saturday in East Lansin...
articles.body:
The Nebraska Cornhuskers are undefeated following the walloping they gave to the Michigan State Spartans Saturday in East Lansing. Favored by 5.5 points, the Huskers dominated the home team, recording six sacks and three takeaways en route to a 31-13 road win.

In truth, the game wasn't even that close.

While Sparty took an early three point lead, it was seemingly all Nebraska the rest of the first half. Anthony Colandrea showed his arm strength. Kwazi Gilmer showed his ability to adjust his body in stride and reel in a big touchdown. It set the tone for the game, as Nebraska imposed its will in a few different statistical categories.

While the running game didn't ever really take off (157 net yards with two rushing touchdowns), part of that can be explained by the early departure of freshman phenom Jamal Rule, who suffered an undisclosed injury. He played eight snaps in the contest. Jacory Barney Jr. managed 21 before an injury took him out of the game.

Barney could be back in time for Saturday's game against Maryland, per HCMR:

Rule is a bigger unknown, especially since we don't know the body part, the extent, or really anything. We'll see if he's slated to make a return and if so, how that changes the money line headed into the Homecoming Weekend game with the Terps.

Speaking of the Terrapins, they lost by 51 points to UCLA last week AT HOME! Can you imagine if the Huskers lost by 51 points at Memorial Stadium? There would be a riot. You'd have to go back to World War II for a loss that bad in Lincoln (61-7 to Minnesota on October 13, 1945). In the modern era…I don't know if we want to revisit 2007 Oklahoma State.

So the 51-point loss has put Maryland HC Mike Locksley on the hottest of seats. He will probably make it to the game Saturday, but if there's a similar outcome on back-to-back weeks, Maryland may look for that eject button.

The Nebraska 4-0 (1-0) Cornhuskers take on the Maryland Terrapins Saturday at 3:00pm. The FanDuel Sportsbook opening line has Nebraska as 14.5-point favorites. The over/under is currently at 52.5 points.

articles.title: Deion Sanders’ Alleged Reaction to Julian Lewis Criticism Raises Eyebrows After Colorado Blowout
articles.summary: Life around Colorado football under Deion Sanders rarely stays confined to four quarters. Off-field drama quickly spills onto social media, turning minor dig...
articles.body:
Life around Colorado football under Deion Sanders rarely stays confined to four quarters. Off-field drama quickly spills onto social media, turning minor digital interactions into major news stories. That dynamic hit a new high after Colorado followed a 41-7 blowout loss against Northwestern with a tough 23-13 defeat to Baylor. Soon enough, local creator and CU alum Matt McCall, known online as Moneyline Matt, pointed out a much larger concern brewing behind the scenes.

On X, Matt McCall posted a screenshot showing Coach Prime liking a post that called quarterback Julian Lewis "trash" after the Northwestern loss, which raised some eyebrows. The post quickly vanished from social media, fueling even more speculation. However, the screenshot's authenticity and Sanders' actual intent remain unconfirmed, as online images can easily be edited or tapped by mistake. Still, for fans watching online, it created an immediate headache.

"Just gonna leave this here to show the type of 'leadership' on display in Boulder," he captioned the screenshot.

The post also included part of Deion Sanders' previous comments from his press conference.

"I told y'all he'll be coming around the mountain, so what does that mean?" the Buffs head coach said of Julian Lewis. "He isn't there yet. I can't expect something out of you that's not in you. That's not an insult."

McCall wasn't simply talking about Julian Lewis. His criticism was aimed at what he sees as a culture problem around the Colorado program. He also argued that the constant cameras, social-media attention, and online exposure Deion Sanders once presented as positives have started creating their own headaches.

"You've got people around the program cussing out fans over football terminology, and now this," he added. "At some point, the constant social media nonsense stops being 'exposure' and starts reflecting on how the program is being run. Right now it's ran by children."

The situation with Julian Lewis was already uncomfortable enough without social media getting dragged into it. The former 5-star QB was benched Saturday after a miserable first half against Baylor. He completed 11 of 16 passes for only 75 yards and no touchdowns. Colorado managed just three points with him leading, and he was sacked three times before halftime.

Deion Sanders made the change with Colorado trailing 10-3. Isaac Wilson took over and gave the Buffs something they had been missing. He finished with 156 passing yards and a touchdown, helping Colorado pull even at 13 before Baylor scored the final 10 points.

The benching itself was not a surprise after what had happened the previous week. Colorado had been crushed 41-7 by Northwestern, with Julian Lewis throwing two interceptions. The Buffs committed seven turnovers overall, and the offense fell into a 21-0 hole before halftime. The QB finished that afternoon with 168 yards and one touchdown on 19-of-29 passing.

Deion Sanders was blunt afterward when asked about Julian Lewis and leadership.

"I expect leadership from (certain players). I don't expect that from certain positions," he said. "That's not the makeup of who they are."

Deion Sanders later pushed back against the idea that he was simply tearing down his QB. He explained that he could not expect something from Julian Lewis that he did not believe was currently in him. And after the Baylor benching, he made another point.

"Don't give up on JuJu," he said. "Don't do that. That kid plays with tremendous effort and tremendous heart. He's not quitting, and he's not abandoning anybody. We just needed a change. We needed inspiration at that time, some kind of way."

That sounds like he's trying to make it clear that a temporary change does not have to become a permanent judgment. Still, the online controversy changes the temperature. Whether Deion Sanders actually intended to endorse the "trash" comment is impossible to establish from a screenshot of an alleged like alone. But that distinction may not matter much to the people watching from outside the program.

articles.title: Chicago Bears take over Monday Night Football with Case Keenum as quarterback
articles.summary: The Bears are taking center stage on Monday Night Football.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears lead the Philadelphia Eagles 10-7 at halftime.

Case Keenum led the Bears to a touchdown on the first drive of their game.

In the second quarter, the Bears scored a field goal after intercepting a pass from Andy Dalton in their own endzone at 3rd and Goal.

The Eagles, with Jalen Hurts back in play after a concussion check, responded with a touchdown.

The following is from a previous report.

The Bears are taking center stage on Monday Night Football.

But they'll do it without starting quarterback Caleb Williams .

Here's what to expect from the Bears this Monday night.

With Williams sidelined by a hamstring injury, veteran Case Keenum is expected to get the start against the Eagles.

Tyson Bagent is cleared from concussion protocol and available as the backup.

Keenum hasn't played in an NFL game since December of 2023.

But ESPN's Laura Rutledge says he knows Ben Johnson's offense well.

Before the Bears take on the Eagles at Solider Field, ABC7 got an exclusive behind-the-scenes look at ESPN's Monday Night Football coverage.

"He's been a bit of a coach player out there, player coach, however you want to put it, and now he gets his opportunity to be out there and show what he's got," Rutledge said.

Rutledge says a strong run game could give Keenum room to work.

Former Bear Israel Idonije says the veteran's best chance is to trust what got him here.

"He can't go out there and try to be Caleb Williams . You know, he's a journeyman; he's talented. He's got to go out there and play his game, control the clock, get the guys behind him, take what the defense gives him," Idonije said.

Still, excitement surrounding this team is building across Chicago , and Bears fever is spreading well beyond the city.

"Chicago is such a great city and such a great fan base and such great people in the city. They've been nothing but welcoming for me. They show out; they show support and they love their sports teams," Bears tight end Colston Loveland said.

"This is a Bears town and people love their football and people love their Bears. So, you just feel that throughout and radiating throughout the whole city," tight end Cole Kmet said.

The team is even getting the Hallmark treatment, teaming up with the Hallmark Channel for "Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story."

The new Christmas movie is out next month.

The Monday Night Football spotlight will also shine on Chicago's Latino community.

The Bears are calling the matchup against the Eagles their "Vamos Bears" game, celebrating Latino heritage and the community's deep connection to the team and the city.

Two-time Latin Grammy-nominated Mariachi Herencia de México, which got its start in Chicago, will perform the national anthem.

Then at halftime, a special live performance will trace the history and influence of Latin music in Chicago, and celebrate generations of Latino communities that have helped shape the city.

The Bears will also recognize two local high school standouts: Alison Segarra of Amundsen High School and Alejandro Gonzalez of Dundee-Crown.

They'll serve as honorary captains and head to midfield with the Bears captains for the pregame coin toss.

And fans will be part of the celebration, too, with wearable "Vamos Bears" flags handed out at the gates.

Idonije joined ABC7 Chicago Monday morning to talk about his South Loop bar's watch party.

Former Bears player Israel Idonije talked about Monday Night Football.

Soldier Field's parking lots open at 3:15 p.m. for tailgaters.

articles.title: Tracking TSSAA football's Division II-AAA programs that will play independent
articles.summary: Major dominoes have fallen as several TSSAA football programs have opted to go independent from Division II-AAA. Here's who've made the move.
articles.body:
The TSSAA's Division II-AAA football teams are nearing a critical deadline.

After the TSSAA released classifications for the 2027-2029 cycle on Sept. 22, multiple Division II-AAA football programs announced their intent to play an independent, non-region schedule for the next two seasons. Those schools will be ineligible for TSSAA playoffs starting next season.

Oct. 2 is the final day TSSAA teams can petition their initial classification assignment, either by moving up or electing for an independent, non-region schedule.

Here is a list of schools that have currently made the decision to move independent of DII-AAA.

See our best photos from Ensworth vs Lipscomb Academy TSSAA football game

Division II-AAA teams that have opted for independent schedules

Father Ryan: President Paul Davis reached out to parents on Sept. 27 to announce the school's intention to compete on an independent, non-region football schedule for the 2027-2028 and 2028-2029 seasons.

Memphis University School On Sept. 28, MUS announced its decision to move to an independent schedule.

Christian Brothers: in a joint statement with MUS, Christian Brothers decided it too will play independent from DII-AAA for the next two seasons.

Other Division II schools will move to independent schedule

Christ Presbyterian Academy: On Sept. 22, CPA football was the first program to announce it'd compete as an independent program, pulling itself out of the Tennessee high school football playoffs for the 2027 and 2028 high school football seasons. CPA was moved up to DII-AAA last year because of the TSSAA's success factor. The high school governing body has eliminated that rule and moved CPA down to DII-AA with its recent release of the initial classifications for football.

Clarksville Academy : Director of communications Steven Wilson announced on Sept. 25 that Clarksville Academy's football program would move to an independent schedule for the next two seasons to protect the safety and well-being of its student-athletes. The Cougars play in DII-A.

Mt. Juliet Christian Academy: Another DII-A program, Mt. Juliet Christian Academy announced it would play an independent, non-region schedule for the 2027-29 cycle. The program has forfeited multiple games this season due to low player numbers, and the TSSAA denied its proposal to co-op with RePublic High School on Aug. 17.

articles.title: Eagles vs. Bears Week 3 game thread
articles.summary: The Eagles will face the Bears in Week 3 on ‘Monday Night Football’.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are on the road again in Week 3 for a Monday Night Football matchup against the Chicago Bears .

All eyes will be on how well the Eagles defense can stop Chicago's run game, not only because that's the part they failed to stop in 2025, but also because the Bears are relying on QB3 Case Keenum as their starter. Not that Keenum can't lead this offense, but he's had only one week to prepare for the occasion, and his last regular season game was in December 2023 — it's been awhile. Still, the veteran isn't to be overlooked, and the Eagles defense needs to play more soundly than they've done through two games this season.

Stay on top of every Eagles update and debate every snap with other diehard Birds fans. Game-day discussion is smoother in the SB Nation app.

It will also be a big night for the Eagles offense, specifically for the guys up front. Cam Jurgens and Drew Kendall have one more week of reps under their belts in their new roles, and will hopefully continue to develop. New OC Sean Mannion has added some really exciting elements, but the run game still needs a boost to make it a more complete package. Saquon Barkley is going to play despite suffering a stinger last Sunday, and will try to eliminate the number of negative plays from the ground game.

Hang out here for updates and to chat, celebrate, vent, and argue in the comments! [You should also download the SB Nation app to make it even easier to follow along with the conversation!]

articles.title: Thursday Night Football Ratings Surge As Falcons Beat Packers
articles.summary: Falcons-Packers drew 16.82 million viewers, marking a second straight weekly high. The win proves the team is back on track.
articles.body:
The numbers do not lie, and they are screaming one clear message about the Atlanta Falcons . Thursday Night Football just hit another high mark in Week 3, drawing 16.82 million viewers on Amazon Prime Video. Local over-the-air simulcasts within home markets are included in that figure. It marks the most-watched Week 3 edition of the show since 2016. This is not just a random bump in the road. The ratings surge coincided with Michael Penix Jr.'s return and Atlanta's 35-14 win over Green Bay .

Fans tuned in because they wanted to see if the offense could finally work. They got their answer on a Thursday night that felt like a playoff game. The broadcast peaked with 19.05 million viewers in the 9:30 PM ET quarter-hour. That is a massive jump from last year's Week 3 matchup between the Dolphins and Bills. Sports Media Watch stated the average for the season's initial two weeks is now 17.94 million. That is up 5% from the same point last year. Prime's median age this season is slightly higher than previously, at 48.0. Viewers among adults 55+ is up 6%, helping push Prime's median TNF viewer age from 47.4 to 48. The surge proves that when the Falcons play with confidence, the whole country watches.

The story on the field was even better than the story on the screen. Michael Penix Jr. went 16 of 18 for 234 yards and a touchdown after shaking off rust. He had a career high in snaps under center and passes between the numbers. Bijan Robinson was the engine that drove this machine. He ended with 213 total yards and two touchdowns. According to The Falcoholic , Robinson has become the 10th player in NFL history to accumulate 6,000 scrimmage yards before turning 25. He is on pace to shatter the franchise record by 400 yards. This offensive explosion made the game a must-watch event. The defense helped too, with CJ Henderson forcing three incompletions and only giving up 40 yards on 11 targets. The team looked like a real operation on a short week.

There is a catch in the data that shows how hard it is to measure modern viewership. Amazon said Monday that the previous week's Lions-Bills audience was re-processed by Nielson because of an error in Amazon's lineup. Similar revisions have occured previously, including the Super Bowl and last season's Brazil game. The Super Bowl and a game in Brazil also saw similar issues. Despite the technical glitches, the trend is undeniable. The Falcons are no longer the last team in every ranking list. NFL Spin Zone moved them up to 29th after they were dead last just a week ago. The arrow is pointing up for the first time in years. With competent quarterback play, the NFC South looks wide open. The fans know it, the numbers show it, and the rest of the league is taking notice.

articles.title: Everything Pat Fitzgerald said prior to playing Wisconsin
articles.summary: See what Pat Fitzgerald's Monday press conference entailed ahead of playing Wisconsin.
articles.body:
Michigan State football has dropped two games in a row, falling to 2-2 and needing to do a ton of soul searching before they travel to Madison in a week.

When they get to Madison to face off with the Wisconsin Badgers , Pat Fitzgerald is going to need to get a very different version of his team, one that is going to limit mistakes and play to their strengths in a Big Ten matchup.

Ahead of that game, like every Monday, Fitzgerald spoke to the media about the state of his team:

"Everyone knows Saturday was not acceptable. You can't win Big Ten games losing the turnover battle 3-0, with other plays that should've been turnovers."

"I don't care about feelings. I care about production, and when we don't produce. We have to eliminate those 15 plays where we don't execute, produce."

"Didn't play complimentary football the last two weeks."

"Joe (Rossi) and Max (Bullough) are doing really well with the group. Those two (DiMari Malone and Adam Shaw ), their future is bright."

"When we brought in Jaz Patterson, we told him we had a guy we wanted as starter, he would be 1B. Jaz said 'I'll make an impact.'"

"I'm not mad at Chuck for the penalty. There was no whistle, the quarterback was still running."

"The penalty with Kenny, we can't have that, players losing their cool."

"That was a catch, but I guess it wasn't."

"Our rush lane discipline was non-existent. When we did what we came to do, we were efficient. Gonna have the same challenge this week, and for the rest of the schedule."

"I want to see them work. I wish it was an easy road, but it's not. Football's not. You're going to get knocked down. We need to get up and go to work. That's the Michigan State way."

"In the pass game, there were times we got hung up on a downfield release. We had guys open that we didn't hit. The big sack fumble, Bull (Rod Bullard) is wide open. Les owned it right after the game."

"We are four games in with this group. It's not an excuse, it's a reality. We need to make good decisions."

"For us, we cannot continue to do what we are doing and expect to win a Big Ten game. We got to be better in all three phases."

"You can tell this is a Luke Fickell team. They're tough, they're physical. Their defense played lights out on Saturday."

"I'm proud of both of our guys (Wright Jr. and Vincic for stepping up). The battle Luka had to go through, all offseason."

"It all goes back to preparation. He (Andrew Brinson IV), Luka, Robert, Shaw, they will go back and prepare more, because they got their taste of the arena. I saw our guys that were in there, did they execute perfectly? No. To see them step up, we're proud."
